text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday before leaving for a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin that enlarging NATO was a top priority but he also wanted a "robust" NATO-Russia partnership.

Clinton, speaking to reporters at the White House, said: "We are adapting NATO to take on new missions, enlarging NATO to take in new members, strengthening NATO's partnership with non-members and seeking to build a robust partnership between NATO and Russia."
Clinton said that relationship should "make Russia a true partner of the (Western) alliance."

The president, who is getting round on crutches or in a wheelchair following surgery last Friday on an injured right knee, leaves later on Wednesday for Helsinki where he will meet Yeltsin on Thursday and Friday.

"We will focus on three important areas. First on moving forward with our work to build a Europe that is undivided, democratic and at peace for the first time of the history of the continent," he said. "Second on continuing to reduce the danger of weapons of mass destruction and third on expanding the economic partnership that is good for Americans and Russians alike," he said.

He said he and Yeltsin would discuss the outline of a NATO-Russia charter to establish the basis of their future relationship. "I believe NATO and Russia should consult regularly and act jointly whenever possible ..." he said.
